free_tier.stated: Event Horizon NX 01 Storage 1 TB G2 at USD 6.99/month: 1 Intel core shared, 2,048 MB RAM, 1,000 GB HDD, 3,000 GB/month bandwidth, 1 Gbps port, IPv4 + IPv6, Oradea Romania. The tracker's line reads "starting at $6.99 per month". The sibling rows move the traffic and not the disk: USD 7.99 buys the same 1 TB disk and 2 GB with 4,000 GB/month, and USD 8.00 buys a 60 GB NVMe White Neptune plan with 2,048 GB/month.

egress.terms: 3 TB a month on the cheapest plan, 4 TB on the USD 7.99 sibling, stated as a plan line; no overage rate and no post-quota policy published on the page read

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: KVM with root and an own AS211462 network, sold through a live client catalog the vendor does not render into the page HTML, so the price and the order path both sit behind a client area; no API documented on the page read.
record.chaining: 1 TB of HDD for USD 6.99 a month is the most disk per dollar among evaluated providers, and it is the only plan here with a disk large enough to matter for the 20 TB dataset; the 3 TB a month is what makes it an ingest target rather than a serving host, and the single shared core is enough to run a transfer agent and nothing else.

limits.value: 3,000 GB a month against a 1,000 GB disk is 3 writes of the disk per month, so the plan can be filled but not served; 3,000 GB is 100 GB a day, 10 percent of the 1 TB daily transfer ceiling.
